item.content:encoded:
Education Minister Francis Siune presented a K5 million dummy cheque to Hela province yesterday to boost Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE) infrastructure across the province.

Under the funding package, Hela's four districts — Koroba-Lake Kopiago, Magarima, Komo-Hulia and Tari-Pori — will each receive K1 million to upgrade their FODE facilities. The remaining K1 million has been allocated to the Pai Hope Institute for the construction of a new Information and Communication Technology (ICT) laboratory.

Minister Siune was with delegation including Education Secretary Dr. Uke Kombra, FODE Principal Anthony Rayapen, First Assistant Secretary for FODE and Inclusive Education Andrew Angobe, and First Assistant Secretary for Projects and Procurement Malon Acquino. Joined by Hela Governor Philip Undialu, the Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu and other distinguished guests.

Commending Governor Undialu's administration for making distance learning a provincial priority, Minister Siune linked the educational investment directly to provincial peace efforts, noting that the ongoing gun surrender program provides a vital opening for transformation.

"Hela should be competing in education, business and other meaningful pursuits — not violence and tribal conflict," Minister Siune said. "When Hiroshima and Nagasaki were bombed by the US during the Second World War, Japan did not retaliate with arms; it focused on becoming a prosperous nation. That is the exact path Hela must take."

He emphasized that the Marape-Rosso Government remains focused on creating second-chance pathways for school dropouts and students unable to secure tertiary placements and is giving priority to supporting FODE across the country.

Governor Undialu supported the Minister's message, urging parents, guardians and community leaders to actively encourage out-of-school youth and school leavers to enroll at FODE and TVET institutions.

"The Government is building the pathways. There is no longer any excuse for a student in Hela to be left behind," Governor Undialu said.

item.title: Tripartite MoU with focus to develop Gulf
item.description: A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding signed recently paves way for new business opportunities in the Gulf Province. Gulf Papua Energy Limited, BNG Trading Company Limited and APEK Resources Development and Freight Services Limited from the Baimuru LLG put ink on paper to give birth to a consortium called Koine Logistics Operating Waterways Limited (KLOW).
item.content:encoded:
A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding signed recently paves way for new business opportunities in the Gulf Province.

Gulf Papua Energy Limited, BNG Trading Company Limited and APEK Resources Development and Freight Services Limited from the Baimuru LLG put ink on paper to give birth to a consortium called Koine Logistics Operating Waterways Limited (KLOW).

All three parties will hold 33.3 percent ownership operating as Koine Logistics Operating Waterways.

The joint venture will provide waterway access, freight and other logistical services needed for Papua LNG, with the potential to support additional developments in Gulf Province.

BNG will act as the operating company through Blue Planet Logistics Limited, responsible for the consortium’s business management and operational affairs.

According to BNG Executive Chairman John Wallace, the MoU now allows the consortium to present to Exxon Mobil, prior to the official announcement next month, December.

“KLOW combines local ownership with proven operating capability, ensuring that the Papua LNG Project is supported by the communities that live along its routes,” Wallace said.

“Working together, I think we have a lot of opportunities and I think our timing is very good. Our timing will give us the chance now to present to Exxon before the announcement in December.”

“Our work is to begin to get our entity in order so we can start engaging with our project at the earlier stages.”

APEK Chairman Steven Ravi described the agreement as a massive opportunity for landowners and communities in Baimuru.

“The Papua LNG Project cannot progress its major development operations without access to the project site.”

Our river system is the primary access route to this major project, and the agreement signed gives land and waterways owners a special privilege and opportunity,” Ravi said.

Gulf Papua Energy Limited Executive Chairman Rendle Rimua said the agreement marks the beginning of a partnership, which also ensures that the Papua LNG Project is supported by the communities that live along its routes.

He praised APEK for joining forces with BNG, noting the company’s extensive experience in PNG.

item.title: Resource landowners in Amanab sustain future through cocoa farming
item.description: Resource landowners of Amanab Blocks 1 to 4 Forest Management Area in Vanimo-Green River district are taking their economic future into their own hands, shifting from logging royalties to sustainable cocoa farming. More than 20 villages in the remote Amanab area are now participating, with farmers already harvesting beans and expanding their plantations.
item.content:encoded:
Resource landowners of Amanab Blocks 1 to 4 Forest Management Area in Vanimo-Green River district are taking their economic future into their own hands, shifting from logging royalties to sustainable cocoa farming.

More than 20 villages in the remote Amanab area are now participating, with farmers already harvesting beans and expanding their plantations.

The initiative follows an agreement between the PNG Cocoa Board and the landowners, supported through Project Development Benefits (PDB) from 2022 to 2024 to establish cocoa in the project area.

In a major boost for farmers, 15 new cocoa fermentary kits purchased from Agmark in Wewak were shipped to Vanimo yesterday for distribution to Amanab. Another 15 kits plus materials for cocoa nurseries are expected to arrive from Lae soon.

According to Cliff Kolu Cocoa Board Project Officer, the fermentary kits were funded by the resource landowners themselves - a sign of their commitment to the industry.

Representing Block Three of the Amanab FMA, landowner leader Bill Wamisa says the mindset has changed.

"Communities are beginning to see cocoa farming as a sustainable activity that can provide economic opportunities for generations to come. We cannot depend on logging forever," Mr Wamisa said.

"More than 20 villages are now actively participating. We have started harvesting and we are expanding our plantations."

Mr Wamisa said with funding support from PDB and technical assistance from the PNG Cocoa Board and the EU-STREIT Programme, close to 16 farmers are now formally registered as cocoa farmers, with many more showing interest.

"This is new for Amanab. Logging was our main income, but now people are realizing cocoa is our future," he said.

However, he said challenges remain with road access and markets.

"Our biggest problem is road. We need proper road access to bring our beans out and to get markets. We are calling on our local MP and the West Sepik Provincial Government to support us with roads and market access."

PNG Cocoa Board Provincial Manager in Vanimo, Gabriel Kipan, says the Amanab project is progressing well, but needs stronger government backing.

"The project is moving, but we need greater commitment from the provincial government and administration to sustain and expand production," Kipan said.

"In 2024, we signed a Memorandum of Agreement between the West Sepik Provincial Government and the PNG Cocoa Board. We are still waiting for the administration to implement that agreement to support initiatives like Amanab."

Kipan said West Sepik Province is targeting 5,000 metric tons of cocoa by 2030, and Amanab can contribute significantly.

He revealed that almost 3,500 metric tons from farmers in Nuku, Aitape and Lumi have already been sold to buyers in East Sepik, showing the potential.

In a positive step, two cocoa depots - West Sepik Investment and Wilyete Cocoa Depot - were established in Vanimo in 2024, enabling cocoa to now be shipped directly through the Vanimo Port.

"That is a big change. Our cocoa can now go through Vanimo Port. That is the future for West Sepik," Kipan said.

Resource owners say with continued support, cocoa will replace logging as the long-term economic backbone for Amanab.

item.title: Commissioner confirms seized round is military weapon
item.description: Police have confirmed that an artillery round seized in Port Moresby on October 29 is a 130mm military projectile. Police Commissioner David Manning said the projectile had been safely extracted and secured, while investigations into its discovery continue.
item.content:encoded:
Police have confirmed that an artillery round seized in Port Moresby on October 29 is a 130mm military projectile.

Police Commissioner David Manning said the projectile had been safely extracted and secured, while investigations into its discovery continue.

He said the round was examined by the RPNGC Bomb Unit and PNG Defence Force Explosive Ordnance Disposal personnel, including through X-ray examinations to confirm its structure.

Commissioner Manning said the discovery was a serious matter and warned the public against speculation that could interfere with the investigation.

He said the investigation would take its course and would not be influenced by public commentary or social media speculation.

“Investigations are conducted by Police, not through social media posts,” he said.

He added that the ordnance had been identified, rendered safe and placed in a secure facility.

Commissioner Manning said investigators were pursuing all avenues of inquiry, with further information to be released at an appropriate time.

item.title: Police officer wanted
item.description: Assistant Commissioner of Police NCD and Central Command, Benjamin Turi is appealing to Port Moresby residents to report to police the whereabout of a suspect police officer identified in the shooting. The officer is alleged to have pulled the trigger on a civilian just outside the Raibow Eliseo shopping center in Port Moresby on Monday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Commissioner of Police NCD and Central Command, Benjamin Turi is appealing to Port Moresby residents to report to police the whereabout of a suspect police officer identified in the shooting.

The officer is alleged to have pulled the trigger on a civilian just outside the Raibow Eliseo shopping center in Port Moresby on Monday afternoon.

Commander Turi says, the Constabulary will not tolerate ill-discipline officers, hence the matter will not be taken lightly.

He says, the suspect officer is also alleged for transgression within the force.

He added that the suspect is currently at large and alleged to have in his possession a R-P-N-G-C issued pump action rifle and is considered dangerous.

“We already put report to Provincial Police Commander Alotau and Oro, with police on the lookout for him including the driver of the vehicle. Victim has reported the case and he is expected to be charged for attempted murder and face the courts” Turi said.

ACP Turi has urged the public to report to police first should they sight him anywhere in the nation’s capital.

“IF anyone comes across him, do not go near, call the police and we’ll deal with him directly. Public must not approach him” Turi said.

item.title: Government remove fuel subsidy
item.description: The government’s 1billion kina fuel subsidy package is now fully exhausted and will be completely removed by 8th of this month, this Sunday. This was announced by the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (ICCC) in a public notice in Port Moresby today.
item.content:encoded:
The government’s 1billion kina fuel subsidy package is now fully exhausted and will be completely removed by 8th of this month, this Sunday.

This was announced by the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (ICCC) in a public notice in Port Moresby today.

This will see price increase of petrol, diesel and kerosin. Consumers, service providers and businesses will dig deeper into their pockets, as fuel costs increases for the month of November.

This follows the announcement by ICCC, that the National Government will remove the fuel relief subsidy and will come into effect this Sunday 8th, November.

The 1billion kina fuel assistance came into effect in April 2026, which the government supported fuel prices through two measures: a direct fuel subsidy to help keep retail pump prices lower; and an exemption from Goods and Services Tax or GST.

In a public Notice, ICCC says the fuel subsidy is now used up and will be removed, in accordance with National Executive Council (NEC) Decision No. 225/2026. However, Government's exemption from Goods and Services Tax will remain until December 31, 2026.

ICCC explains the change to the subsidy arrangement is a fiscal policy decision made by the Department of Treasury as part of the Government’s management and reprioritisation of public expenditure. ICCC does not determine government tax or subsidy policies.

The consumer watchdog says international fuel prices have increased, while the removal of the subsidy and the weakening Kina against the US dollar will add further pressure on pump prices that sees increase fuel prices for this month.

ICCC adds this is the ripple effect of the ongoing middle east war and also government has reprioritized its spending due to conflicting priorities, especially the El Niño assistance.

Meantime, ICCC will review regulated PMV and taxi fares in December 2026 to determine whether any adjustments are needed.

However, the expected rise in fuel prices from November 8 will not automatically increase transport fares, as any changes must go through a separate regulatory process.

item.title: Hagen market to reopen on Monday
item.description: Mt Hagen's main market, also known as the food basket of the Pacific, will reopen to the public on Monday, November 9, after remaining closed for nearly three weeks following a death linked to an incident inside the market. The closure has disrupted the livelihoods of hundreds of farmers, market vendors, producers and consumers who depend on the market for their daily income and food supplies.
item.content:encoded:
Mt Hagen's main market, also known as the food basket of the Pacific, will reopen to the public on Monday, November 9, after remaining closed for nearly three weeks following a death linked to an incident inside the market.

The closure has disrupted the livelihoods of hundreds of farmers, market vendors, producers and consumers who depend on the market for their daily income and food supplies.

The market also provides an important trading space for subsistence farmers and small-scale sellers who rely on it to support their families.

However, following a 'bel-kol' compensation arrangement by the market board and management with the deceased's tribe, tensions have eased, paving the way for the market to reopen.

The deceased was from the Jika Palga tribe, whose councillor, Michael Paul, has confirmed the tribe's position on the reopening.

"As the ward member of Kunka Palga tribe, I have released and agreed to reopen the gates of Hagen Market for normal business."

"We leave now everything on the hands of the police, the market management and the board and assures that no one in my tribe or community would do anything in the market," Paul says.

Meanwhile, Wamp Nga Group of Companies chairman and Hagen Rural LLG president, Paul Pangum, says the prolonged closure has affected many people but should also serve as a lesson to the market management.

Mr Pangum stressed management must improve its operations, strengthen security and ensure the market provides better services to the public.

He says the new management, under Hagen Two Investment manager Peter Noki, will introduce changes to the market's administration, management and workforce.

" Now with the new market management, as the Chairman of the market board I would want to see the removal of the old workforce and incision of new ones and also for the market management to work closely with the police and councillors to control and minimize law and order issues in and around the Hagen Market."

Mr Pangum has apologised to farmers, vendors and consumers affected by the closure, saying he shares their concerns and regrets the hardship they have faced.

He assures market users that changes will be made to improve the market's operations once it reopens on Monday.

He has also challenged Mr. Noki to enforce the new measures firmly and manage the market without fear or favour.

Earlier this week, the Mt Hagen main market management met with councillors representing the affected tribes and police to discuss the way forward for the market's operations.

The reopening of the market will gradually see a restoration for a major trading centre for Mt Hagen and surrounding communities, while the new management faces the challenge of ensuring the market operates safely, efficiently and in the interests of all market users.

item.title: Independent panel to look into UPNG allegations
item.description: The University of Papua New Guinea council in its meeting today, announced the appointment of an independent investigation panel to look into the allegations of “unacceptable conduct” in its administration. This after Professor Ian Findlay voluntarily resigned last week alleging ongoing unacceptable conduct by Chancellor Sir Robert Igara, who was in turn asked to step down by Prime Minister James
item.content:encoded:
The University of Papua New Guinea council in its meeting today, announced the appointment of an independent investigation panel to look into the allegations of “unacceptable conduct” in its administration.

This after Professor Ian Findlay voluntarily resigned last week alleging ongoing unacceptable conduct by Chancellor Sir Robert Igara, who was in turn asked to step down by Prime Minister James Marape.

Students held a sit in protest yesterday (Tuesday 03.11.26) calling for the immediate reinstatement of Findlay and resignation of Sir Robert.

The council also formally announced the appointment of Acting Chancellor Goiye Gileng and Acting Vice Chancellor Professor Betty Lovai.

In a media statement this afternoon, Mr. Gileng says the special council meeting also formally received the complaints and allegations of the former VC and accepted the “voluntary leave of absence” by Igara pending the outcome of the independent investigation.

Gileng has assured students, parents and stakeholders that the council is in control and its business as usual.

The Acting Chancellor is expected to immediately submit a report of the actions taken to the Minister of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology.
